observed_mechanics: 0x00c30c80: MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX + 0xb0] is the only field read; the whole function is a projection of that one 32-bit id.
0x00c30c86/0x00c30c89: CMP EAX,-0x1 / JZ -1 is an explicit invalid-id sentinel: it short-circuits to the zero return without touching any global.

0x00c30c8b/0x00c30c8c: the id is pushed and 0x00b3d2a0 is called. That callee is exactly MOV EAX,dword ptr [0x0167eae4] / RET, so it ignores the pushed word and returns the global handle table; because its RET is bare the pushed id stays on the stack.

0x00c30c91/0x00c30c93: the pushed id is therefore the stack argument of 0x00ba6d80, which is __thiscall with one 4-byte argument (RET 0x4) and resolves it: handle 0 returns [table + 0x14c], handle -1 returns 0, and any other handle is looked up in the two-level table at [table + 0xc8] with page = handle >> 12 and slot = handle & 0xfff.
0x00c30c98/0x00c30c9a: an unresolved handle yields the zero return.

0x00c30c9c/0x00c30c9e: the resolved handle is passed in ECX and control is tail-transferred with JMP, not CALL, so 0x00bba500's return value is this function's return value and no cleanup is inserted.

0x00bba500 is itself a lazy accessor with a cache: [owner + 0x80] is reused only when [cached + 0x504] == [owner + 0x74], otherwise 0x00401090 and 0x004df550 re-resolve it; a zero id returns the cache directly and a failed re-resolve calls 0x00bba2a0 first.

semantic_contract: Resolve the 32-bit record id stored at this+0xb0 to a record pointer. An id of -1 is the unset sentinel and returns 0 without touching any global. Otherwise the id is pushed, the global handle table at 0x0167eae4 is fetched by a two-instruction getter, and the handle is resolved through that table (handle 0 is a dedicated field at +0x14c, handle -1 resolves to 0, anything else is a page/slot lookup). A zero resolution returns 0. A non-zero resolution is tail-transferred to 0x00bba500 and that function's result is returned unchanged, with no post-processing in this body.
subsystem: Resolves the 32-bit record id at this+0xb0 through the global handle table at 0x0167eae4 and tail-transfers the result to the cached record accessor 0x00bba500, returning 0 for the -1 sentinel or an unresolved handle.
classification_rationale: Every instruction, field offset, constant, global and branch polarity is read directly from the 13-instruction body, and the three callees are read directly as well (one of them, 0x00ba6d80, resolves the handle table layout). It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because two material elements stay bounded: the owning class of the +0xb0 field is not identified in any of the 15 callers, and the domain meaning of the id, of the handle table and of the returned record is not established - the 0x4e0-stride record shape is shared with 0x00c04750, but nothing in the binary names the record type.
semantic_findings: The function is a two-level indirection: an id field on the receiver is resolved through a global handle table before any record is touched.
The -1 sentinel is checked on the receiver's own field, so an uninitialised owner costs one compare and never reaches the global.
The final call is a tail transfer, so the record accessor's cache-validation logic is the only place where the record is obtained and this function adds no semantics of its own beyond the two guards.
0x00bba500's cache is validated by comparing an id field inside the cached record, so a stale cache is detected by data comparison rather than by any generation counter.
unresolved_questions: Which class owns the +0xb0 id? All 15 callers pass a different receiver and none of them identifies the owner in a way that can be checked statically.
What does the id denote, and what is the record type? The returned record is read at +0x4ec as a 3-float vector by one caller and at +0x504 as an id by 0x00bba500, but no name for it is established.
What are the semantics of the 0x00bba2a0 call in the zero-id and failed-lookup paths? Its body was not decompiled in this batch.

The handle table's page stride of 20 bytes for 4096-entry pages is unusual (five pointers per outer entry); whether the outer table is really indexed by page was not cross-checked against a writer of that table.
Whether the value at 0x0167eae4 is a singleton or is re-assigned during play is unobserved: the file image holds zero.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists for this address.
The record type, the handle table and the meaning of the +0xb0 id can only be settled with a runtime trace that shows the resolved record in use.
